keyboard.description: A computer input device used to enter text, numbers and commands.
components: Cable or wireless battery if present
hazards: Wireless models may contain batteries.
Circuit boards should not be burned.
Dust or residues can collect between keys.
safety: Unplug before cleaning.
Remove only user-removable batteries.
Do not burn or dismantle electronics without suitable training.
reusable: Cable or receiver in good condition
recommendation: Otherwise send to an authorized e-waste collection or recycler.
disposal: Keep separate from ordinary mixed waste where e-waste collection is available.

battery.description: A device that stores electrical energy. Exact chemistry depends on the battery type.
materials: May include lithium compounds, nickel, lead, steel, aluminium and plastics depending on chemistry.
components: Battery management circuitry in some packs
hazards: Fire, short circuit or chemical leakage if damaged.
Some chemistries contain hazardous substances.
safety: Never puncture, crush, burn or short-circuit.
Do not handle swollen, hot, leaking or damaged batteries; seek professional guidance.
Follow the collection facility's transport instructions.
reusable: Only batteries assessed as safe and serviceable by a qualified professional.
repair: Do not open sealed battery packs yourself. Ask a qualified technician to assess them.
recommendation: Use a battery take-back scheme or authorized battery/e-waste recycler.
disposal: Do not place loose batteries in fire or regular trash; follow local battery collection rules.

laptop.description: A portable computer containing processing, storage, display and power components.
hazards: Lithium-ion batteries can be hazardous if damaged.
Stored personal data may remain on drives.
safety: Back up and securely erase data before transfer.
Do not puncture or open a battery pack.
Ask a professional about swollen or damaged batteries.
reusable: Compatible RAM or storage after assessment
repair: Ask a technician about battery, storage, RAM, keyboard or display repair.
recommendation: Repair, refurbish or donate if safe and functional; otherwise use an authorized e-waste recycler.
disposal: Use a recycler that can safely manage batteries and data-bearing storage.

mobile phone.description: A handheld communication device with a display, cameras, electronics and rechargeable battery.
hazards: Lithium-ion battery may catch fire if damaged.
Personal data may remain on the device.
safety: Back up data, sign out of accounts, remove SIM and memory cards, and securely erase data.
Do not puncture or remove a glued-in battery yourself.
repair: Ask a qualified technician about screen, battery or charging-port faults.
recommendation: Repair, trade in, donate or refurbish if functional; otherwise use a take-back scheme or authorized recycler.
disposal: Do not put phones in general waste; use a dedicated collection route.

charger.description: A power adapter that supplies electricity suitable for a compatible electronic device.
hazards: Damaged insulation can cause electric shock.
Burnt, cracked or unusually hot chargers may be unsafe.
safety: Disconnect before inspection.
Do not open mains adapters.
Replace damaged chargers with compatible certified products.
reusable: Undamaged charger that works with the intended device.
repair: Have repairs performed by a qualified service.
recommendation: Reuse if safe and compatible; otherwise use e-waste collection.
disposal: Do not open the adapter or place it in mixed waste where e-waste collection is available.

mouse.description: A pointing device used to control the cursor on a computer.
hazards: Wireless models may contain a battery.
Circuit boards should not be burned.
safety: Disconnect before cleaning.
Remove only user-replaceable batteries.
repair: Check sensor, cable, receiver or battery; replace only compatible parts.
recommendation: Reuse or donate if working; otherwise use e-waste collection.
disposal: Keep separate from general waste where e-waste collection is available.

monitor.description: An electronic display used to show computer output.
hazards: Broken screens can cause cuts.
Older display technologies may need specialized handling.
Do not open the power supply.
safety: Do not break the screen or open the power supply.
Transport carefully to avoid damage.
reusable: Working monitor, stand and cables after inspection.
repair: Have screen, power and connector faults checked by a qualified technician.
recommendation: Reuse or donate if functional; otherwise use an authorized e-waste recycler.
disposal: Do not break the display or leave it at an informal dumping site.

circuit board.description: An electronic board that connects and supports electronic components.
uses: Controlling or processing electrical signals in devices
materials: Electronic components and small amounts of various metals
hazards: Some boards or components may contain substances requiring controlled processing.
Cut edges may be sharp.
safety: Do not burn, sand or chemically treat circuit boards.
Use trained handling for damaged assemblies.
reusable: Tested compatible boards or components after professional assessment.
repair: Diagnosis and component replacement require appropriate electronics skills.
recommendation: Use a specialist e-waste recycler with circuit-board recovery processes.
disposal: Do not burn boards or recover metals with household chemicals.

headphones.description: An audio accessory that converts electrical signals into sound.
hazards: Wireless models may contain rechargeable batteries.
Damaged cables may expose conductors.
safety: Disconnect wired headphones before cleaning.
Do not open or puncture a wireless battery.
reusable: Working headphones, cable or compatible earpads.
repair: Check cable, connector, earpads or battery with a qualified technician.
recommendation: Reuse or donate if functional; otherwise use e-waste collection.
disposal: Do not place wireless headphones with built-in batteries in general waste.
